headline: A big sell-off in AI and chip stocks overnight points to a lower start for Nifty after Thursday's jump to 25,514. The question for today is whether foreign buyers step in on the dip, as they have done for 8 days running.

mood.label: Negative
mood.why: Global markets point to a weaker open, while the dashboard's own checks lean up (score +30, 3 of 4 checks agree), so today looks like a dip inside an uptrend. Overnight data as of 08:46 IST; NSE data from Thursday's close.

key_points.text: GIFT Nifty (the overnight Nifty price traded abroad) was near 25,315, about **200 points lower** than Thursday's close, after the Nasdaq fell 2.25% and Asian chip-heavy markets fell 4–6%.
FIIs (foreign funds) bought a net **₹7,411 crore** of Indian shares on Thursday, their 8th day of buying in a row. Reports say they are moving money out of AI-heavy Korea and Taiwan and into India.
My call: a lower open, with the fall more likely to slow during the day than to turn into a deep slide. Confidence is medium, because Asian markets are down unusually hard.
Not everything overnight was bad: gold fell about 5% and US bond rates eased, while crude oil barely moved at about **$92.5**.

sections.title: What changed overnight
sections.summary: The night brought clearly worse news for the open, and it goes against Thursday's 1.1% rise.

points.text: US stocks fell hard: S&P 500 down **2.0%**, Nasdaq down 2.25%. Reports blame selling in AI stocks, as Nvidia slid 3.3% despite strong results and Anthropic's market debut did not lift the sector.
US futures are down a little more this morning (S&P −0.4%, Nasdaq −0.8%), so the selling has not stopped yet.
Asia is falling sharply: Taiwan **−6.0%**, Korea −4.6%, Japan −4.5%, Hong Kong −2.1%, Shanghai −1.9%. These markets hold many chip makers, so they feel AI selling most.

Gold fell about 5% since India closed to $3,535, a 1-year low, and the US 10-year bond rate eased to 5.01%. Lower US rates make markets like India a bit more attractive. I couldn't confirm why gold fell so much.
Brent crude is flat at $92.5 and the rupee is unchanged at 93.29 per dollar. Infosys's US share fell 1.1%; HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank's US shares were flat.

sections.title: Bounce or continuation?
sections.summary: After a big up day, I expect a pullback at the open, but a full reversal of the rally looks less likely; medium confidence.

points.text: Signs of a pullback: fresh bad news overnight, Asia falling 2–6%, the US fear gauge (VIX) up **16%** to 28, and Nifty just made a 9-month high, which invites profit-taking.

Signs the uptrend holds: FIIs have bought for 8 days, their share of bets on a rise in index futures went up from 32.5% to **34.2%**, and India has little AI exposure, which is why money has been moving here.
Monday is the monthly expiry and Tuesday is a holiday, so traders may cut risk before a long gap with global markets still nervous.
What would prove me wrong: Nifty falling below **25,000** (the biggest floor in the option data) would mean a deeper fall; closing back above 25,500 would mean buyers already took the dip.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.summary: The trend is up, and the dashboard reads bullish with medium confidence.

points.text: Nifty at 25,514 is above its 20-day (24,236), 50-day (23,470) and 200-day (23,991) averages, and is making higher highs and higher lows. Trend check: **+2**, the top score.
Futures price rose and open positions edged up 0.6%, a small sign of new bets on a rise (score +0.6, halved because the change was under 1%).
Options data reads negative (score −1.2): many puts were added at 25,000–25,300, and the dashboard reads these as people buying protection against a fall, not as a floor being built.
The put-call ratio (bets on a fall compared with bets on a rise) jumped from 1.00 to **1.34** in 5 days. The dashboard counts that as support (+1).
India VIX at 15.8 is higher than on 72% of days in the past year, so the market expects bigger swings than usual.

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.summary: Foreign funds are buying heavily while Indian funds sell into it.

points.text: FIIs bought ₹7,411 crore on Thursday, about 1.4 times their normal daily amount. November so far: about **₹1.02 lakh crore** of net buying.
Domestic funds (DIIs) sold ₹1,357 crore on Thursday and about ₹56,900 crore this month. This is the reverse of the usual pattern, where Indian funds buy when foreigners sell.
FIIs still hold about two bets on a fall for every bet on a rise in index futures (34% long). That is far less one-sided than the 14% at the start of the month.

Strategists quoted in news reports call this buying a tactical return after FIIs held too little India, not yet a lasting shift. Reports say FIIs are still net sellers for 2026 as a whole, by about $21.9 billion.

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.summary: US interest rates and AI-stock nerves are the two big worries; cheaper oil is the main help.

points.text: Traders expect the US Fed to raise rates again on 10 December; reports put the chance at about **95%**. Higher US rates tend to pull money away from India.
US bond rates are still very high at about 5% (90th percentile of the past year) and the dollar index is near a 1-year high, which usually makes FIIs cautious.
Brent crude is down **15%** in a month to $92.5. India buys most of its oil abroad, so this cuts costs and helps inflation.
The rupee has firmed 1.2% against the dollar in a month, which makes Indian shares more valuable for foreign buyers.

sections.title: Company results
sections.summary: Results season is mostly over; the main results story today is Nvidia's effect on Indian IT.

points.text: No Nifty 50 company filed results in the past 7 days, so results are not a big driver today.

Nvidia posted strong results but its stock still fell 3.3%, because investors are worried about AI spending and its leadership change. That mood can hit Indian IT, which already fell **1.1%** on Thursday.
Ashok Leyland: revenue up 35% but profit up only 8.8% from last year, an in-line result. Auto stocks rose over 4% on Thursday, so some profit-taking is possible.
Manappuram Finance: profit up **77%** on revenue up 56%, a strong result by the dashboard's rule.

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.summary: A short, holiday-broken week leads into GDP, the RBI and a likely Fed hike.

points.text: Monday 23 Nov: Nifty monthly expiry, then Tuesday 24 Nov is a market holiday, so two days of global news will hit Wednesday's open at once.
30 Nov, 4 pm: India's GDP numbers. Strong growth would back up the FII buying story.
4 Dec, 10 am: RBI rate decision. 10 Dec (around midnight IST): Fed decision, where a hike is widely expected; a bigger-than-expected hike would hurt.
The main risk to the uptrend: if the AI sell-off turns into wider global selling, FIIs may stop buying India even if India itself looks cheaper.

levels.note: A close above 26,000 would push the range higher; a close below 25,000 would break the biggest floor and point to a deeper fall.

watch.text: How big the gap-down is, and whether buyers show up in the first hour.
IT stocks (Infosys, TCS, Tech Mahindra) after the US tech sell-off.
Taiwan and Korea through the day: further falls would keep pressure on.
Evening FII figure: a 9th day of buying would show the dip was bought.

bottom_line: The dashboard reads bullish (score +30, 3 of 4 checks agree), backed by strong FII buying and a clear uptrend. But overnight news is clearly bad: a sharp AI and chip sell-off in the US and Asia points to Nifty opening about 200 points lower. My read is a dip within an uptrend, helped by India having little AI exposure and by falling oil, with medium confidence. The main risk is that the global sell-off deepens and foreign funds pause their buying ahead of the long weekend.
